version.changelog: OpenAI Ads API v1 Marketing Agent with Habilis MCP Gateway integration

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent ads-management tool, but it asks for powerful ad-account and tracking authority with under-scoped privacy and credential-safety controls.

dimensions.detail: Using an API key and outbound API calls is expected for an ads API client, but one bundled client reads an undocumented OPENAI_ADS_BASE_URL override and sends the bearer token to that destination without origin validation. The docs also under-disclose privacy implications for CRM webhooks, lead forms, pixels, CAPI events, and hashed customer identifiers.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is presented as a normal skill install with local Markdown references and Python scripts; I found no install-time hooks, package-install commands, obfuscated payloads, or automatic startup behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The playbook tells the agent to manage the full ad lifecycle, pause losing ad groups, scale winners, publish lead forms, wire CRM webhooks, and configure conversion tracking, but it does not define approval gates, spend boundaries, rollback expectations, or consent checks before high-impact actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no evidence of OS-level persistence, but the skill is designed to create durable external objects such as campaigns, ads, spend settings, tracking pixels, CAPI tokens, lead subscriptions, and business agents. Those persistent business and tracking effects need explicit user control.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised purpose matches the artifacts: managing ChatGPT/OpenAI ads, campaigns, creatives, budgets, lead forms, product feeds, pixels, CAPI, and insights. That same scope is high-impact because it can affect advertising spend, public ad content, lead data flows, and tracking setup.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Only use it with a least-privileged ads API key, fixed trusted API origin, explicit per-action approval for campaign creation, budget changes, publishing, pausing/scaling, and tracking setup. Do not enable lead webhooks, CRM sync, pixels, or CAPI events until you have confirmed consent, data minimization, retention, destination security, and key-rotation procedures.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Environment-supplied credentials and network calls are expected for an ads API automation skill, and SKILL.md discloses OPENAI_ADS_API_KEY usage. The concern is partially supported because the artifact lacks a clear permissions/trust-boundary section and does not require confirmation before credentialed API actions.
[SQP-2] expected: README.md advertises lead-sync webhooks, CRM integration, web pixels, and server-to-server conversion tracking. These are purpose-aligned, but the finding is supported because the README does not explain consent, data minimization, retention, webhook security, or third-party sharing risks.
[SQP-2] expected: SKILL.md similarly describes lead capture, webhooks, CAPI tokens, and conversion events while only briefly addressing client-supplied credential storage. It does not give enough sensitive-data or privacy guidance for lead and attribution workflows.
[RA2] expected: Pixels, CAPI events, lead subscriptions, and CRM pipelines are expected in an ads-management skill, so this is not rogue behavior by itself. It remains a review concern because these features can persistently track and forward user interaction data without documented opt-in controls or retention limits.
[T09] unexpected: The static scan concern is supported for scripts/openai_ads_client.py: it reads OPENAI_ADS_BASE_URL and attaches Authorization: Bearer OPENAI_ADS_API_KEY to requests without validating scheme or host. That override is not needed for normal production use and is not disclosed in the setup instructions.
